```markdown
# Roadmap — sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), uv workspace. Azure services per the ADR (status Proposed; acceptance is §7 step 1).
Ranking: given 2026-11-06, list order.

| # | Outcome | Spec | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes for a chosen range, downloaded and kept as received | R1, §2.1, §4.2 | 1 | ~2 requests per quarter (listing + file), about 260 for 1993 onward, under 2 min at 3 req/s (§4.8); bytes measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | New daily indexes picked up on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed days | R2, §2.1, §4.2 | 2 | ~250 files a year, one request each plus listings; negligible at 3 req/s |
| O3 | A Parquet filing-index dataset, one row per filing, built from those indexes | R3, §4.4, §4.5, §4.6 | 3 | measured by Stage 1 |
| O4 | The whole pipeline running on the Azure services the ADR names | R4, §4.1, §4.7, §4.9 | 4 | Azure spend measured by Stage 7; §2.2 makes no cost guarantee before measurement |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation runs share one downloader, parser and publisher | R5, §4.1, §4.2 | 5 | no material cost |
| O6 | A parser change rebuilds the dataset from stored originals with no new download | R6, §4.3, §4.5 | 6 | raw storage equal to O1 + O2 bytes; measured by Stage 1 |
| O7 | Periodic re-reads of quarterly indexes that pick up SEC corrections | R7, §4.2, §4.4 | 7 | each run re-fetches every supported quarter: O1's bytes per week (§4.8) |
| O8 | All SEC traffic held to one shared request budget, however many workers run | R8, §4.3 | 8 | caps all SEC throughput at the configured rate |
| O9 | Readers see only complete, versioned quarter datasets through one active pointer | R9, §4.5, §4.6 | 9 | no material cost |
| O10 | No filing leaves the catalog without explicit approval tied to the source hash | R10, §4.4 | 10 | owner time per gated quarter |
| O11 | Schedules, retry limits and rate target held as reviewed starting configuration | R11, §4.8, §5 | 11 | no material cost |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Open questions

- The repo has four scaffolded packages (`sec-edgar-client`, `-download`, `-index-ingest`, `-ingest`), and a root script pointing at a nonexistent `sec_edgar` module. §4.9 names one package, `sec-edgar-ingest`. Settled in Stage 1's brainstorming.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Local quarterly baseline
      Objective: Turn a small range of real archived quarterly indexes into a Parquet filing index on a local machine.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: an owner-chosen quarter range and SEC User-Agent identity (§4.8)
      Produces: quarterly downloader and parser; Parquet output in the §4.5 row contract; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — the range's quarterly master indexes are stored byte-for-byte as received. O3 — a Parquet dataset whose row count per quarter matches the source data-line count. Findings record the real run's bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory and observed request rate.
      Leaves out: manifests (Stage 3); traceability (Stage 3); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7); full validation suite (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily ingestion and catch-up
      Objective: Add daily indexes through the same download and parse path as the baseline.
      Outcomes: O2, O5
      Consumes: Stage 1 downloader, parser and Parquet output
      Produces: daily discovery with catch-up across quarter boundaries; one shared collection/parse path
      Exit: O2 — a run from a handoff date across a quarter boundary ingests every listed daily file; a rerun after a skipped day catches up; an empty listing reports `no_new_sources`. O5 — backfill and daily runs call one downloader and one parser; no second implementation exists.
      Leaves out: manifests (Stage 3); traceability (Stage 3); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7); full validation suite (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Raw snapshots, manifests and replay
      Objective: Record sources, snapshots and processing state so that any output can be rebuilt from stored bytes.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stages 1–2 collection and parse path
      Produces: manifests and traceability per §4.5; content-addressed raw storage; resumable checkpoints per source
      Exit: O6 — a parser-version bump rebuilds output from raw storage with zero SEC requests, and a rerun on unchanged hashes does no work.
      Leaves out: point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7); full validation suite (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: One SEC request budget
      Objective: Make every SEC request, from any run, go through one leased, throttled collector.
      Outcomes: O8
      Consumes: Stages 1–3 collector and manifests
      Produces: shared lease and request budget (§4.3), used by every SEC-facing command
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill and daily collectors never exceed the configured rate together; lease loss stops new requests before a successor issues any.
      Leaves out: point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7); full validation suite (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Publish each quarter as a complete generation behind a conditional active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 3 manifests
      Produces: point-in-time awareness per §4.6: generations, manifests and the active pointer readers resolve
      Exit: O9 — under injected crashes before files finish, before the pointer moves and just after, a reader sees only complete generations; a competing publisher cannot overwrite a newer pointer.
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 7); full validation suite (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly sources and apply their changes, gating any removal on hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 2 shared path; Stage 3 manifests; Stage 4 request budget; Stage 5 publication
      Produces: reconciliation command; change reports; approval records
      Exit: O7 — a corrected quarterly fixture publishes its additions and updates, recorded in the change report. O10 — a closed-quarter candidate that drops keys stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval naming its hash; open-quarter absence withdraws nothing.
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 7); full validation suite (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure orchestration and deployment
      Objective: Run the shared commands on the ADR's Azure services in an isolated environment, with triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: ADR and spec accepted (§7 step 1); Stages 1–6 commands; Stage 1 findings for sizing
      Produces: scheduling and deployment (versioned infrastructure, ADF pipelines and schedules, disabled); full validation suite (§6 CI and integration tests)
      Exit: O4 — in the isolated environment, §7 steps 3–5 pass and their smoke-test record is written; every §6 exit criterion passes in CI. The measured Azure cost of the smoke run is recorded.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Reviewed configuration and production operation
      Objective: Fix the reviewed starting configuration, then run the baseline and enable scheduled operation.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stage 7 deployment and smoke-test record
      Produces: release record (image digest, configuration revision, active generations); runbooks (§8)
      Exit: O11 — invalid configuration is refused before any network I/O (§5), and the §4.8 values are recorded in a reviewed revision; §7's Exit list is met with observed scheduled runs.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run derive-roadmap §6 over the Outcomes list, with evidence per verdict. Also list as unmet each numbered spec requirement that no outcome's `Spec` cell cites (none at writing: R1–R11 are all cited). Each unmet item becomes a new stage or a written deferral.
```

---

The roadmap's eight stages follow your O1–O11 ranking except where dependencies force a change: O3 joins O1, because downloads alone are not a working outcome. O5 rides with O2. O8 comes before O7's reconciliation traffic. O4 (Azure) moves to Stage 7, so that the local stages' measured volumes inform its sizing. Do you approve this partition, so I can commit it on `main` and hand off Stage 1 to brainstorming?
